Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with wheeze and shortness of breath.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Symptoms have been present for 2–3 days.
Patient feels feverish but temperature is 37°C.
Symptoms have not been waking the patient at night.
Patient experiences shortness of breath on walking.
Sometimes it is hard for the patient to complete sentences due to shortness of breath.
Patient is currently well at rest.
Patient reports no exercise tolerance recently.
Patient does not have a peak flow meter.
Patient does not have a spacer.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of childhood asthma that was quite bad.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: PMH: Childhood asthma (quite bad; occasional hospital visits, no ICU; missed school)

Past_Medical_History.content: Childhood asthma required occasional hospital visits but no ICU admissions.
Childhood asthma caused the patient to miss school.

Medications.content: Patient uses salbutamol inhaler as needed every few weeks.
Medications.source_text: Meds: Salbutamol inhaler PRN (every few weeks; uses with exercise “a bit”)

Medications.content: Patient uses salbutamol inhaler with exercise a bit.
Patient is on no other medications.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks approximately one glass of wine every 2–3 days.
Patient has been working from home or on sick leave for the last few days due to shortness of breath.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: WFH/sick leave last few days due to SOB

Assessment.content: Asthma exacerbation supported by 2–3 days of wheeze and shortness of breath, cough, exertional dyspnea, and occasional speech limitation.
Assessment.source_text: 2–3 d wheeze/SOB, cough, exertional dyspnea, occasional speech limitation

Assessment.content: Asthma exacerbation assessment notes afebrile status with temperature 37°C and absence of sputum, hemoptysis, or chest pain.
Past medical history is significant for asthma in the context of current exacerbation.

Plan_of_Care.content: Increase short-acting beta agonist: salbutamol 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Increase SABA: salbutamol 2–4 puffs q4h initially

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe spacer and have pharmacist demonstrate its use.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate use

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe peak flow meter and have pharmacist teach its use.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Prescribe peak flow meter; pharmacist to teach

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient to record morning and evening peak flow values for one week.
Safety net advice: call back urgently if high temperature or worsening wheeze.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety net: call back urgently if high temp or worsening wheeze

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange asthma review in approximately one week.
Consider additional inhaler after asthma review.
For allergic rhinitis, start regular over-the-counter antihistamine.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Allergic rhinitis: start regular OTC antihistamine (per note in chart)

Follow_up_Information.content: Asthma review planned in approximately one week.
Patient advised to call back urgently if high temperature or worsening wheeze.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Safety net: call back urgently if high temp or worsening wheeze

Physical_Findings.content: No other vitals or physical examination findings documented.

Review_of_Systems.content: Patient reports feeling feverish but with measured temperature 37°C.
Symptoms have not been waking the patient at night.
